REJB 1998-05906 - Texte
intégral

CITATION: K. (D.) v. U. (L.)

Cour
supérieure
(Chambre de la famille)

CANADA

PROVINCE DE QUÉBEC

DISTRICT DE Montréal

NO : 500-12-224372-957

DATE :  1998-04-09

EN PRÉSENCE DE :

John Bishop
, J.C.S.

K. (D.)

Plaintiff

v.

U. (L.)

Defendant

Bishop:-

1. The Procedures:

1
Mr. K.
presents a motion dated June 5, 1997, and amended on March 2, 1998, to modify
his rights of access to the parties' son, B., as established by the judgment of
divorce of December 20, 1995, which confirmed two consent agreements of the
parties. The amended conclusions of Mr. K., motion read as follows:

A
. THAT Plaintiff have access to and visit with the parties' minor
child, B., every two out of three weekends from Friday, after school, to
Sunday, 7:00 p.m., in addition to every Wednesday evening from after school
until Thursday morning when Plaintiff will return Bradley to school. In the
event of a statutory holiday or a professional day, the access in all cases
would be extended by twenty-four hours;

B
. THAT Plaintiff have access to and visit with B., four weeks during
the summer vacation, that is, two non-consecutive two week periods;

C
. THAT with respect to the winter vacation, that is, during the
Christmas period, Plaintiff shall have access to and visit with B., for half
the period of time that the parties have as vacation; for example, if the
parties have ten days off work, then Plaintiff shall have access to and visit
with B. for a period of five days or, alternatively, that Plaintiff have access
to and visit with B. every second year for the entire Christmas vacation,
commencing the Christmas vacation of December 1998 to January 1999;

D
. THAT the Spring vacations, that is, in February as well as April,
shall be split among the parties equally; however, if Passover falls, as it
will this year, on the Spring break in April 1998, then Plaintiff will have B.
during the Spring break in April.

E
. THAT Plaintiff have access to and visit with B. each year on the eve
of Rosh Hashonah and the following two days of Rosh Hashonah, the eve of Yom
Kippur, as well as the following day of Yom Kippur, in addition to the evening
prior to the first day of Passover as well as the first two days of Passover following
that evening;

F
. THAT with respect to the access during summer and the Christmas
holidays, Plaintiff shall have the right to take B. out of the Province of
Quebec upon giving Defendant two weeks' prior notice in writing and, in
exercising this rights of access and visitation in the summer time, Plaintiff
will provide Defendant with two weeks' prior notice for each of the two weeks
consecutive periods in writing;

G
. THAT Plaintiff shall have access to and visit with B. on Father's Day
when it does not fall on one of his week-ends and, as well, on Plaintiff's
birthday, whenever that may be; and

H
. THAT with respect to B. birthday, which is January 24
th
, Plaintiff shall
have access to and visit with B. for an equal amount of time that Defendant spends
with B. on that day.

2
Mrs. U.
presents three motions:

1. Her amended
motion of September 2, 1997 to increase to $1,007.41 per month the alimentary
pension of $150 per week payable by Mr. K. for B. under the divorce judgment;

2. Her motion of
November 25, 1997 to modify Mr. Karp's rights of access to B. as follows:

1. ORDER that
Plaintiff has the first night of Rosh Hashannah, Yom Kippur, and Passover, to
be alternated each year, as of 1998. The first night of these holidays belongs
to Plaintiff for 1998. This will alternate each year and the child is to be
returned home that same evening;

2. ORDER that the
child B. will always spend the week of Christmas with Defendant;

3. ORDER that the
child B. will always spend the week of New Years with Plaintiff;

4. ORDER that
Plaintiff will have the child for (the) last full week of July and ORDER that
the Defendant will always spend the following week of August with the child;

3. Her motion of
June 20, 1997 for a provision for costs of $3,000.

3
An interim
order of November 28, 1997 permitted Mr. K. to take B. to Florida from December
25, 1997 to January 3 or 4, 1998.

4
Pursuant to
the parties' agreement of November 10, 1994, as confirmed by the divorce
judgment, Mrs. U. was given legal custody of B., and Mr. K. was given the
following rights of access:

1. Every second
weekend, from late Friday to Sunday evening;

2. Every Wednesday
from the end of school until bedtime at Mrs. U.

3. On the high
Jewish holidays, namely Rosh Hashana, Yom Kippur and Passover, for one day
until B. bedtime;

4. On Mr. K.
birthday and Father's Day, and for half of B birthday; and

5. During the
parties' vacation days in winter and summer, each one will have equal time with
B.

5
The
agreement provided that B. could not be taken out of Quebec “for any
period of time” without the written consent of the party not accompanying
him.

II. The Questions at Issue:

6
These are:

1. (a) Has there
occurred, since the divorce judgment, a change which would justify a
modification of Mr. K. rights of access?

(b) If so, what
modifications would be appropriate?

2. (a) Has there
occurred, since the divorce judgment, a change which would justify a
modification of B. alimentary pension?

(b) If so, what
modification should be made?

3. Is Mrs. U. entitled
to a provision for costs, and, if so, in what amount?

III. The Parties and their Means:

7
The parties
were married on July 16, 1989, and have been separated since September 7, 1994.
The divorce judgment was rendered on December 20, 1995.

8
B. is 7 years
old and attends grade one at school. He lives with his mother.

9
Mr. K., is
33. He works full time during the week. The proof does not disclose his present
income. According to his employer's letter of August 27, 1997 (D-3), in 1997 he
received a gross weekly salary of $885 and a weekly car allowance of $105, for
a gross total of $51,400. He has remarried on October 18, 1997, and his new
wife is expecting a child.

10
Mrs. U. is
33. She works full time during the week. Her gross income, including a
conditional bonus of $2,425, was $32,000 in 1997 (P-2). She remarried on June
22, 1997. This remarriage appears to have been a motivating factor in Mr. K.
motion, which was served on June 10 and presentable on June 23, 1997.

11
After
interviewing the parties and B. on November 14, 1997, Mr. K. psychologist, Abe
Worenklein, prepared a report recommending increased rights of access for Mr.
K. (P-1), but not recommending that Mr. K. obtain custody, as he had originally
requested in his motion of June 5, 1997. The interviews were carried out prior
to Mr. K. remarriage.

IV. Modification of Access Rights?

12

Sec. 17(5)

of the
Divorce Act
reads:

17
. ... (5) [
Factors for custody order
] Before the court makes a
variation order in respect of a custody order, the court shall satisfy itself
that there has been a
change in the condition, means, needs or other
circumstances of the child
of the marriage occurring since the making of
the custody order or the last variation order made in respect of that order, as
the case may be, and, in making the variation order, the court shall take into
consideration only the best interests of the child as determined by reference
to that change.

(underlining added)

13
What
change has occurred since the divorce judgment in the “conditions, means,
needs or other circumstances” of B. which would justify the granting by
the Court of a modification order?

14
In
Willick
vs. Willick
(1994)
1994 CanLII 28 (SCC)
, 3 S.C.R. 670 , the Supreme Court of Canada stated, at p.
688:

In deciding whether
the conditions for variation exist, it is common ground that the change must be
a material change of circumstances. This means a change, such that, if known at
the time, would likely have resulted in different terms. The corollary to this
is that if the matter which is relied on as constituting a change was known at
the relevant time it cannot be relied on as the basis for variation.

15
In the
Court's opinion, the proof does not disclose any such material change. The
remarriages of the parties have not as yet changed B. situation in either
household.

16
Mr. K.
argues that B. is more than two years older, and, therefore, needs to see his
father more often. However, the Court believes that this argument does not, in
itself, constitute an adequate justification for a modification of access. The
proof does not indicate that, if B. had been two years older at the time of the
divorce, more generous rights of access would have been given to Mr. K.

17
Even if
such a material change had occurred in B. situation since the divorce, the
Court believes that the proof does not show that it would be in B. best
interests at the present time to spend two out of every three weekends with his
father.

18
The
differences between the parents as to access rights of Mr. K. essentially concern
only the division between them of the Jewish holidays and of the summer
vacations, as well as the right of each parent to take B. on short holiday
trips outside Quebec at specified times without the prior consent of the other
parent, as required by the divorce judgment.

19
The Court
attempted unsuccessfully at trial to have the parties reach agreement on these
minor matters. Neither the parties nor their attorneys showed any interest in
resolving their disputes, despite the negative effects caused thereby to B. The
parties appeared to give their personal vendetta, using B. as a pawn, priority
over the best interests of their child.

20
The
voluminous correspondence between the attorneys from March 9 to April 8, after
the case was taken under advisement, confirms this unfortunate situation.

21
Even if a
material change had occurred in B. situation since the divorce, in the Court's
opinion, the evidence at trial was insufficient to establish what, if any, new
formula for the sharing of the Jewish holidays and the summer holidays would be
in B. best interest.

22
These
minor adjustments in access rights should be settled by agreement between the
parties, taking B. best interests into consideration.

23
Mrs. U.
has expressed her concern about Mr. K. attending, with the latter's father,
certain sporting events at B. school, where B. is participating. Mrs. U. feels
threatened when B. talks to Mr. K. and his grandfather on these occasions.

24
In the
Court's opinion, it is in B. best interest that his father continues to be
involved in B. school activities and that contact be permitted between them on
these occasions. Mr. K. behaviour as a spectator during these activities should
not presently cause Mrs. U. to feel threatened.

V. Modification of Alimony?

25
Sec. 17(4)
of the divorce Act reads:

17.
.... (4) [
Factors for child support order
] Before the court
makes a variation order in respect of a child support order, the court shall
satisfy itself that
a change of circumstances as provided for in the applicable
guidelines has occurred
since the making of the child support order or the
last variation order made in respect to that order.

(underlining added)

26
Under sec.
2(1) of the Act, the “applicable guidelines” are defined, as
regards the parties in the present case, as those of Quebec. The Quebec
Guidelines do not specify what change of circumstances is envisaged by sec.
17(4), although sec. 14 of the Federal Guidelines does so.

27
Under sec.
14(c) of the Federal Guidelines, the mere fact that the previous order was
rendered prior to the coming into force of the Guidelines is a sufficient
change of circumstances. Under both guidelines, alimony payable for B. under a
new order is no longer taxable in Mrs. U. hands. This fact alone constitutes a
material change, even if there is no significant change in the amount of the
award. Furthermore, B. orthodontic expenses are a new need on his part. Neither
Mr. K. nor Mrs. U. contested the latter's right to claim alimony for B. under
the new guidelines.

28
In
Lavoie
vs. Paré
, C.S. n
o
700-12-12748-877, a judgment rendered by Mr. Justice Senécal on
February 25, 1998, he stated:

II (art. 14 of the
Federal Guidelines) constitue néanmoins une très précise
indication devant servir (in Quebec) à l'interprétation de la
Loi
sur le divorce
quant à l'intention du législateur
fédéral.

29
In
Vincent
vs. Lussier
, C.S. n
o
540-12-003617-866, a judgment rendered on February 4, 1998 by Mr.
Justice Dalphond of the Superior Court, he stated that

... l'entrée
en vigueur d'une nouvelle méthode de calcul des pensions alimentaires,
accompagnée d'une défiscalisation de celle-ci constitue des
circonstances nouvelles justifiant, au sens de l'art. 594 C.C.Q., un
réexamen de la situation des parties ...

30
See also
Gabriel
vs. Osselyn
C.S. n
o
505-12-011756-932, a judgment of Mr. Justice Verrier rendered on April
6, 1998.

31
The child
support determination form of February 26, 1998 (D-1) is probably the most
accurate, as regards the parties' revenues, of the three forms filed. It shows
a basic parental contribution (line 401) of $7180. According to Mrs. U.
testimony, and supporting exhibits, annual child care expenses for B. (line
403) are $2,053, and his school, day camp, hockey, soccer, and Y.M.C.A. special
expenses (line 405) total $1,589. These three amounts total $10,822.

32
Mr. K.
share of these expenses, calculated at 65.4%, is $7,075, or $590 per month. Mr.
K. should also pay his share (65.4%) of any necessary orthodontic expenses
incurred, and to be incurred, by B. (D-4).

VI. Provision for Costs:

33
Mrs. U.
claim of $3,000 is made pursuant to Rule of Practice no. 36 in family matters,
which reads:

36
. The Court may at any stage of the proceedings order a party to pay to
the other a provision for costs.

34
Pursuant
to
art. 25(2)
of the
Divorce Act
, this rule of practice,
inter alia
, is
applicable in divorce matters (
c.f. D.F. no. 605

1989 CanLII 367 (QC CA)
, 1989 R.J.Q. 505 ,
C.A.).

35
Our Courts
consider that a provision for costs is of an alimentary nature and is
accordingly subject to the rules governing the granting of alimentary pensions,
despite the fact that it is usually payable in a lump sum.

36
Mrs. U.
motion alleges merely that Mr. K. has caused “severe financial
hardship” to her by serving his motion, “as well as necessitating a
motion for contempt of court due to his obsessive and continuous
harassment” of Mrs. U.

37
No motion
for contempt of court has been filed in the record by Mrs. U. , nor was any
adequate proof made as to Mr. K. harassment of Mrs. U. Furthermore, no proof
was made as to the legal expenses incurred by Mrs. U. in connection with the
present motions. If Mrs. U. has in fact incurred significant legal expenses, it
is more likely that they are related to her three motions, which (except for
that claiming alimony under the new guidelines) are unfounded, as is that of
Mr. K.

38
The Court
does not believe that it should encourage further litigation between the
parties, which is not in B. interest, by awarding a provision for costs.

39

Accordingly, in the Court's opinion, the motion for a provision for costs
should be dismissed.

VII. Conclusions:

For these Reasons, The Court:

40
1.
Dismisses Mr. K. amended motion for modification of his access rights;

41
2. Grants
Mrs. U. motion for an alimony order under the new guidelines, and modifies the
divorce judgment by ordering Mr. K. to pay alimentary support of $590 per month
to Mrs. U. for B. only, payable in advance on the first day of each month, or
in accordance with law, from and after April 1, 1998, and subject from and
after 1999 to the indexation provided by law;

42
3. Orders
Mr. K. to pay to Mrs. U. upon demand 65.4% of any and all necessary orthodontic
expenses incurred by her for B. , whether past, present or future, less
payments on account thereof received by her from her insurer;

43
4.
Dismisses Mrs. U. motion for modification of the access rights of Mr. K.;

44
5.
Dismisses Mrs. U. motion for a provision for costs;

45
6. Orders
provisional execution of this judgment, notwithstanding appeal.

46
Each party
paying his or her own costs.

Bishop

Me Philip Fine
, for plaintiff.

Me Norman S. Kessner
, for defendant.
